To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
testosterone had a small effect on weight gain, which was similar in the absence or presence of GH.
testosterone has no effect on IGF-1 and IGF-1 receptor mRNA levels in the liver and the growth plate, but does affect GH receptor mRNA levels.
testosterone had no effect on growth mediatores of the GH- IGF-I axis at the level of the liver or EGP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of testosterone, in the absence and presence of GH, on growth mediators in the liver and the EGP.
the mechanism whereby testosterone promotes growth in the juvenile male rat.
the mechanism whereby testosterone may affect growth in the juvenile rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
testosterone has a small effect on growth, and this effect is mediated through an unknown mechanism.
testosterone does not have a direct growth-promoting effect on growth, at least as assessed by the parameters studied here.
testosterone exerts its effect on growth through a complex and poorly understood mechanism, which is not mediated by IGF-I or IGF-I receptor in the liver and the EGP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
testosterone has no direct, GH-independent, effect on the growth-promoting mediators of the IGF-I axis in either the liver or the epiphyseals.
testosterone has a small but significant effect on linear growth in rats that is not mediated by the GH-IGI-I axis.
testosterone has little effect on the GH-IGFI axis in juvenile rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
testosterone does have a small but significant effect on weight gain and that this effect is not mediated by IGF-I.
testosterone does not have a direct, IGF-I-mediated effect on growth, but it may have an indirect, GH-mediated effect on growth.
the effect of androgens on growth is not mediated by the classical IGF-I axis.
